text: Taliban releases biography of reclusive founder Mullah Mohammed Omar to dispel rumors of his death. Document asserts Omar remains the group's leader and details his early military career. Analysts suggest the move aims to bolster leadership credentials amid the rise of ISIS.

Hundreds gathered in South Carolina Saturday for the funeral of Walter Scott, a Black man fatally shot by a white police officer. The service served as a call for racial justice and systemic change following the release of a bystander's video of the shooting. Officer Michael Slager faces murder charges, though witnesses provide conflicting accounts of a struggle prior to the gunfire.

Former TSA agent Daniel Boykin was sentenced to six months in jail and five years of probation for secretly filming a female colleague in a restroom. Boykin also pleaded guilty to aggravated burglary and computer violations after police found thousands of illicit images and videos of the victim.

Cape Verde is leveraging its rich musical heritage to drive economic growth and diversify its economy. The government and private sector are promoting international festivals and networking events to boost global exposure. These efforts aim to stimulate the creative economy and increase tourism revenue.

Arsenal beat Burnley 1-0 via an Aaron Ramsey goal to move within four points of league leaders Chelsea. The result keeps the Gunners' title hopes alive ahead of next week's pivotal clash. In relegation battles, Aston Villa beat Tottenham 1-0 while Sunderland suffered a 4-1 loss to Crystal Palace.

Original *Twin Peaks* cast members have launched a #SaveTwinPeaks campaign supporting David Lynch in a salary dispute with Showtime. Lynch recently exited the planned nine-episode revival, citing insufficient funding to execute his vision. Showtime says it still hopes to bring both creators back for the project.

Andrew Getty, 47, grandson of oil tycoon J. Paul Getty, has died of apparent natural causes at his home. Los Angeles police report no evidence of foul play, citing the heir's history of several health issues. An autopsy is pending.

Maryland police are holding Nyia Parler, 41, pending medical treatment before her extradition to Philadelphia. Parler is accused of abandoning her quadriplegic son in a park for several days to visit a boyfriend. The victim was discovered Friday suffering from dehydration and malnutrition.

NASA astrophysicist Amy Mainzer has named asteroid 316201 after Pakistani education activist Malala Yousafzai. Mainzer cited the need to honor women of color and the importance of global female education in the naming.

CDC investigating gastrointestinal illness affecting 100 passengers and crew aboard the Celebrity Infinity. The ship is scheduled to meet agency officials in San Diego on Monday. Celebrity Cruises has increased disinfection procedures while the cause of the outbreak remains undetermined.

Weekly trends include the digital HD release of the "Star Wars" saga and Nina Dobrev's departure from "The Vampire Diaries." Other highlights feature Mindy Kaling's brother admitting to faking his race for medical school and Burger King sponsoring a wedding for a couple with the same names.

FBI charged a Philadelphia woman for attempting to travel overseas to join ISIS. Two New York women were also arrested this week for allegedly planning a domestic bombing. The arrests highlight a rise in decentralized terror threats and recruitment via social media.
HBO released a teaser for "True Detective" season 2, premiering June 21. The new season stars Colin Farrell, Vince Vaughn, Rachel McAdams, and Taylor Kitsch in a conspiracy plot set in California.

Carlos Colina, 32, has been charged with assault and improper disposal of a body after human remains were found in a duffel bag and apartment building in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The victim was identified as 26-year-old Jonathan Camilien. Authorities are awaiting medical examiner results to determine if further charges are warranted.

Trey Moses, a star basketball recruit at Eastern High School in Louisville, Kentucky, has gone viral after asking Ellie Meredith, a freshman with Down syndrome, to be his prom date. The gesture highlights the school's "Best Buddies" program, which fosters friendships between students with and without developmental disabilities.

NBC debuts "A.D. The Bible Continues" this Sunday, following the early days of Christianity. Other notable premieres and returns include "Marvel's Daredevil" on Netflix and the final episodes of "Mad Men" on AMC. FX also launches "The Comedians" and a new season of "Louie."

Indiana Gov. Mike Pence faces backlash after signing a controversial religious freedom law allegedly aimed at boosting his conservative credentials for a 2016 presidential run. The move signals a broader rightward shift among GOP candidates seeking to appeal to ultraconservative primary voters. Similar legislation in multiple states suggests LGBT rights will remain a central "cultural war" issue in the upcoming election.

Apple released a mobile OS update introducing diverse emoji options for race, ethnicity, and sexual orientation. The move aims to better reflect global demographics but has sparked mixed reactions. Some users and groups continue to lobby for further inclusions, such as specific hair colors and national flags.

Avril Lavigne revealed she was bedridden for five months after contracting Lyme disease. The singer described a severe struggle to breathe and move before recovering at home. Lavigne is now returning to music with a new single.

New research from the Anne Frank House indicates Anne and Margot Frank died at least a month earlier than previously recorded. Evidence suggests the sisters succumbed to typhus before February 7, 1945, contradicting the official March death date.

Two Troy University students were arrested for the gang rape of a woman during spring break at Panama City Beach, Florida. The charges follow the discovery of a video during an unrelated shooting investigation. Both suspects have been suspended from the university.

A one-year-old dog in Washington State survived being hit by a car, struck with a hammer, and buried alive. The dog, named Theia, is receiving extensive veterinary care for jaw and sinus injuries funded by public donations.

FBI confirms death of most-wanted Malaysian bomb maker Marwan following a January raid in the Philippines. The operation resulted in the deaths of 44 elite Philippine police officers and strained a regional peace agreement. Marwan, a member of Jemaah Islamiyah, has been removed from the FBI's Most Wanted Terrorists list.

Criticism mounts over Obama administration's nuclear framework with Iran, alleging the deal trades critical sanctions leverage for insufficient concessions. Opponents argue the agreement allows Iran to maintain nuclear infrastructure and lacks the "anytime, anywhere" inspections needed to prevent a future bomb.

AMC's "Mad Men" returns Sunday for its final season. The series concludes its exploration of 1960s advertising and cultural disintegration. Plot speculation centers on character exits and the impact of the era's shifting social landscape.

A giraffe named Katie gave birth to a calf Friday evening at the Dallas Zoo. The event was streamed live by Animal Planet via 10 cameras. The newborn's gender and condition were not immediately disclosed.

Loretta Lynch's nomination for attorney general faces a record-breaking Senate delay. Supporters and civil rights activists allege racial bias, while Republicans attribute the hold-up to partisan disputes.

Three dead and five wounded after armed assailants stormed the attorney general's office in Balkh province, Afghanistan. Victims include two police officers and one security guard. Security forces are currently engaged in an ongoing firefight to neutralize the attackers.
Bob Barker returned to host "The Price Is Right" for the first time in eight years on April 1. The 91-year-old legend hosted the "Lucky Seven" game before handing duties back to Drew Carey.
Blues legend B.B. King has been discharged from the hospital after being treated for dehydration linked to Type II diabetes. The 89-year-old musician is now resting at home.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev found guilty on all counts in Boston Marathon bombing. Author argues that radicalization is driven by political grievances and exploitation rather than the Islamic faith itself. Suggests community engagement and non-violent activism as the primary tools to combat extremism.

CNN's weekly video roundup features a tour of Mike Tyson's former Ohio mansion and footage of the world's fastest "giga-coaster." Other highlights include an exclusive interview regarding sexual assault allegations against Bikram yoga creator Bikram Choudhury and an eyewitness account of the Germanwings crash.

Pentagon map shows coalition forces reclaimed 25-30% of Iraqi territory from ISIS. Expert Afzal Ashraf notes gains are primarily from conventional frontal pushes rather than disruptive maneuverist warfare. Ashraf suggests ISIS is using asymmetric attacks and propaganda to mask strategic losses.

A passenger on an Air Canada flight from Toronto to Atlanta was allegedly attacked with a headphone cord by another passenger. The suspect was escorted off the plane by U.S. authorities and taken for medical and mental evaluation. The FBI is reviewing the incident for potential charges.

Former banker Rurik Jutting faces two counts of murder after police found two Indonesian women dead at his Hong Kong apartment. One victim was found on the floor and another inside a suitcase on a balcony. A court hearing to determine if the case will proceed to trial has been adjourned until May.

Multiple tornadoes swept through the rural Midwest on Thursday, leaving one person dead in Fairdale, Illinois. Significant property damage was reported across Illinois, Iowa, and Missouri, including the destruction of dozens of homes in Ogle County. Authorities credit National Weather Service warnings for preventing further casualties.

Don McLean's original manuscript for "American Pie" sold for $1.2 million at a Christie's auction Tuesday. The 16-page draft marks the third-highest price ever paid for an American literary manuscript.

UNRWA Commissioner-General Pierre Krähenbühl will visit Syria's Yarmouk refugee camp Saturday to assess a dire humanitarian crisis. The mission follows reports of malnutrition and safety threats to 18,000 civilians trapped by fighting between government forces and militants.

Saudi-led coalition airstrikes and ground fighting in Yemen have killed an estimated 600 people and crippled infrastructure in Houthi-held areas. The ICRC is calling for an urgent humanitarian ceasefire as medical supplies remain grounded. Meanwhile, the security vacuum has allowed al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula to expand its influence.

Former Australian cricket captain and legendary broadcaster Richie Benaud has died at 84. A record-breaking leg-spinner and captain, Benaud gained global fame as a peerless commentator for both Australia and the BBC. Prime Minister Tony Abbott has ordered flags to fly at half-mast in his honor.

Western North America is viewing a total lunar eclipse this morning, the shortest of the century at under five minutes. The event is the third in a rare four-part "tetrad" series. Partial views are visible across the U.S. and parts of Asia and South America.

Federal grand jury charges real estate heir Robert Durst with unlawful possession of a firearm. Durst remains held without bail while awaiting extradition to Los Angeles to face first-degree murder charges. He also faces state weapons and drug charges in New Orleans.

"Furious 7" opens Friday, marking the first major release since Paul Walker's 2013 death. The film uses special effects and body doubles to complete Walker's role in a tribute to the late actor. Co-star Vin Diesel and fans described the release as an emotional farewell.
Model Manuela Arbelaez accidentally revealed the correct price of a car during a "The Price Is Right" episode Thursday. Host Drew Carey awarded the vehicle to the contestant following the blunder.

Thai Smile has unveiled an Airbus A320 featuring "Adventure Time" themed livery and interiors. The partnership with Cartoon Network Amazone promotes a new water park in Pattaya. The themed aircraft will begin flights from Bangkok to Phuket on April 4.

Pedestrians and restaurant patrons in Washington, D.C., helped a mother duck and her brood safely cross a busy street Tuesday. Bystanders used an umbrella to corral the ducklings before guiding the family to a nearby grassy area.

French investigators have completed evidence collection at the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash site in the Alps. Both black boxes were recovered, and DNA profiles have been isolated for 150 victims. Authorities maintain co-pilot Andreas Lubitz intentionally crashed the aircraft.

Cuba and the U.S. attend the Summit of the Americas together for the first time since 1962 amid efforts to restore formal diplomatic ties. Negotiations center on the U.S. potentially removing Cuba from its state sponsors of terrorism list. Tensions persist as Cuba maintains close ties with Venezuela and faces internal dissident clashes in Panama.

Analysis of New Testament texts suggests Jesus' itinerant ministry relied on a common purse for subsistence. Scholars indicate the mission was likely funded through begging, hospitality, and donations from wealthy supporters, specifically women like Mary Magdalene and Joanna.

California regulators ordered PG&E to pay a record $1.6 billion penalty for unsafe gas transmission operations following a fatal 2010 pipeline rupture in San Bruno. Most of the funds are earmarked for pipeline safety infrastructure improvements.

Lauren Hill, a college basketball player who gained global attention for playing despite a terminal brain tumor, has died at age 19. Hill raised $1.4 million for pediatric cancer research and was praised by officials and athletes for her tenacity.

A four-alarm fire broke out Friday morning at the General Electric Appliance Park in Louisville, Kentucky. No injuries or trapped persons were reported. The cause of the blaze remains under investigation.

Iranian Foreign Minister Mohammad Javad Zarif is leading nuclear negotiations with U.S. Secretary of State John Kerry to end sanctions. Zarif is a U.S.-educated diplomat with a complex history, including early revolutionary activism and past U.S. federal investigations. The two officials are working toward a June 30 deadline to finalize a nuclear agreement.

Connecticut judge denies motion to return 17-year-old cancer patient to her mother's custody. The teen remains in state custody at a medical center after being forced to undergo chemotherapy for Hodgkin lymphoma. State officials say she may return home once treatment concludes in April.

New research suggests William Shakespeare and John Fletcher co-authored the play "Double Falsehood." University of Texas scholars used computer software to analyze linguistic patterns, concluding the work was not written by Lewis Theobald.

French prosecutors and investigators deny reports from German and French magazines claiming a cell phone video exists of the final moments of Germanwings Flight 9525. Meanwhile, Lufthansa confirmed co-pilot Andreas Lubitz had a history of severe depression. Authorities are investigating whether fear of losing his pilot's license motivated the crash.

American Samoans, including veteran Emy Afalava, are suing in federal court to secure U.S. citizenship. Plaintiffs argue the denial of birthright citizenship is a racial injustice rooted in outdated Supreme Court precedents. A decision from the D.C. Circuit is expected soon.

Blue Bell has shut down its Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, plant after listeria contamination was found in 3-ounce ice cream servings. The CDC warned institutions to discard specific products from the facility following a linked outbreak at a Kansas hospital. The company is investigating the cause of the contamination.

Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for a deadly attack and hostage situation at Garissa University College in eastern Kenya. The incident underscores deteriorating security in East Africa and the group's ongoing campaign of cross-border raids. Analysts cite regional instability, governance failures, and social exclusion as primary drivers of the group's recruitment and violence.

U.S. officials are filing a diplomatic complaint with Russia after a Russian SU-27 fighter jet intercepted a U.S. reconnaissance plane over the Baltic Sea. The Pentagon described the maneuvers as "unsafe and unprofessional," while Russia claimed the U.S. aircraft was flying toward its border with its transponder off.

Artist Phillip Hyman created a black-winged angel sculpture to mourn the police shooting of Walter Scott in North Charleston. The artwork has since become a symbol for local Black Lives Matter protests.

North Charleston police officer Michael Slager has been fired and charged with murder after shooting unarmed Walter Scott eight times. Bystander video contradicts Slager's claim that Scott attempted to take his Taser. The footage has exposed discrepancies in initial police reports regarding the incident.

ISIS claims control of parts of Iraq's largest oil refinery in Baiji following Saturday's assault. Iraqi security officials deny the claim, insisting government forces maintain full control. The strategic facility is a key domestic fuel source located near Tikrit.

Nashville district attorney bans prosecutors from offering female sterilization in plea deals following public outcry. The move highlights a legal debate over whether such voluntary waivers of constitutional rights are permissible. Analysis suggests the controversy stems from gender bias, as similar sterilization practices for male offenders rarely draw public condemnation.

Ebola infections have dropped to their lowest weekly levels since May 2014, with over 10,000 deaths recorded during the epidemic. While Liberia and Sierra Leone are decommissioning surplus treatment centers, the WHO warns that unknown transmission chains persist in Guinea.

NCAA denies legal responsibility for ensuring academic integrity at member institutions in response to a lawsuit by former UNC athletes. The move draws criticism for contradicting the organization's public claims that student-athlete education is paramount. The NCAA maintains it lacks operational control over university coursework.

Six people were injured after an oil leak triggered an explosion and fire at a paraxylene chemical plant in Zhangzhou, Fujian province. Over 600 firefighters contained the blaze, and no toxic spills were reported. The facility has a history of safety incidents and previous public opposition due to pollution concerns.

Defense attorney argues for mandatory police body cameras following the fatal shooting of Walter Scott by Officer Michael Slager. Author claims cameras would reduce use-of-force incidents and provide accountability against systemic racial bias. Body cameras are presented as a critical interim tool to restore public trust in law enforcement.

Tensions mar the VII Summit of the Americas as Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro accuses the U.S. of coup attempts. Cuba has publicly backed Maduro, complicating the anticipated diplomatic rapprochement between President Obama and Raul Castro.

Fire broke out at Russia's Zvyozdochka shipyard during welding repairs on a nuclear submarine. No injuries were reported and officials say there is no threat to the facility. The vessel's nuclear fuel and armaments had been previously unloaded.

Tropical storm Maysak, known locally as Chedeng, is expected to make landfall in Isabela province on Sunday. Philippine authorities have issued warnings for flash floods and landslides, initiating precautionary evacuations and banning outdoor coastal activities.

NFL legend Deion Sanders publicly mocked his son, Deion Sanders Jr., on Twitter for claiming he only eats "hood doughnuts." The elder Sanders reminded the SMU player of his trust fund and luxury lifestyle, urging him to stop pretending to be from the hood.

Guatemala faces epidemic levels of gender-based violence and femicide, driven by a legacy of civil war, systemic impunity, and deep-rooted machismo. While 98% of cases rarely reach court, new government laws and NGO initiatives are working to empower women and challenge harmful social norms. International attention and action remain critical as millions of women continue to face extreme violence.

Police in Malegaon, India, are requiring cattle owners to provide "mugshots" and physical descriptions to create a livestock database. The measure aims to enforce a state-wide ban on beef sale and consumption by tracking missing animals. Beef traders have responded with strikes and planned legal challenges.

Lucknow police in northern India are deploying pepper-spraying drones to control violent protests and mob attacks. The move has sparked criticism from rights advocates who argue the technology promotes authoritarianism over dialogue. Official launch of the surveillance program is expected later this month.
Christie's sold the original handwritten lyrics to Don McLean's "American Pie" for $1.2 million on Tuesday. The 16-page manuscript was purchased by an unnamed buyer.

London police are investigating a sophisticated heist at a Hatton Garden jewelry vault. Former Scotland Yard official Roy Ramm suggests the raid likely involved meticulous planning and potential inside information. Investigators are now utilizing forensic science and CCTV analysis to track the perpetrators.

7-Eleven will host its first "Bring-Your-Own-Cup Slurpee Day" this Saturday from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Customers at participating U.S. stores can fill any sanitary container fitting a 10-inch opening for $1.49.

Former Kentucky State Senator criticizes Rand Paul's presidential bid, calling his outreach to minority voters "hype." The author argues Paul's record on civil rights and voting legislation is outdated and disqualifying.

A passenger died Sunday after a Lamborghini crashed into a guardrail at the Exotic Driving Experience at Walt Disney World Speedway. The driver, who lost control of the vehicle, was hospitalized with minor injuries. Petty Holdings issued a statement expressing sympathy for those involved.

Defense rested Monday in the murder trial of former NFL star Aaron Hernandez. Prosecutors presented circumstantial evidence including footwear impressions and security footage, while the defense challenged the technical validity of the findings. Closing arguments are scheduled for Tuesday.

Chinese authorities have detained Wu Rongrong and four other women's rights activists for "creating disturbances" after they planned protests against sexual harassment. The detentions occur as Beijing prepares to adopt its first anti-domestic violence law and mark the 20th anniversary of the Fourth World Conference on Women. The activists face formal arrest by April 13.

Former Maryland Gov. Martin O'Malley challenged the "inevitability" of frontrunner Hillary Clinton during a visit to Iowa on Friday. O'Malley urged a robust primary conversation and teased a potential presidential bid despite low polling numbers.

Former pro-football player Aaron Hernandez was sentenced to life in prison Wednesday for the first-degree murder of Odin Lloyd. Family members delivered emotional statements during the Fall River, Massachusetts, court proceedings.

Ted Cruz launched his Iowa campaign by aggressively courting the state's influential evangelical base through religious appeals and defense of religious liberty laws. Cruz aims to build a winning coalition by bridging the gap between evangelical Christians, tea party activists, and libertarians.

Marvel Studios and other producers released a wave of new character reveals and images for upcoming superhero projects. Highlights include the first full look at the Vision in "Avengers: Age of Ultron" and Ben Hardy as Angel in "X-Men: Apocalypse." Additional previews were shared for "Daredevil," "Fantastic Four," and "Deadpool."

Italian Coast Guard rescued 978 migrants off the coast of Libya Friday. Over 10,000 migrants have arrived in Italy since January, with deaths at sea rising sharply compared to last year. Most arrivals originate from West Africa, Somalia, and Syria.

French-language network TV5Monde is recovering from a "powerful" cyberattack that crippled its websites, social media, and 11 channels. While the network has regained some control, ISIS logos appeared on its accounts during the outage. No group has officially claimed responsibility.
Director David Lynch will not direct the "Twin Peaks" revival due to budget disputes with Showtime. The network expressed regret over the decision but remains hopeful for a resolution.

High-profile trials for Dzhokhar Tsarnaev and Aaron Hernandez reach closing stages in Massachusetts. Sen. Rand Paul officially enters the GOP presidential race, while Chicago holds a mayoral runoff. Local elections proceed in Ferguson, Missouri, amid ongoing racial tensions.

Tornadoes and severe storms struck Kansas and Missouri Wednesday night, causing wind damage and flooding. Reports include sightings near Goddard and Aetna, Kansas, and Potosi, Missouri. Further storms are forecast across the Midwest and river valleys Thursday.

Jodi Arias was sentenced to life in prison Monday for the 2008 murder of ex-boyfriend Travis Alexander. Judge Sherry Stephens opted against the possibility of early release. The sentence follows two deadlocked juries regarding the death penalty.

EPA investigating presence of restricted pesticide methyl bromide at a U.S. Virgin Islands luxury villa after a Delaware family of four fell seriously ill. The Department of Justice has launched a criminal probe into the incident. Terminix, the pest control firm used by the resort, is cooperating with authorities.

Columbia Journalism School professors cited "institutional failure" in a flawed Rolling Stone report on a purported UVA gang rape. The magazine issued an apology as the Phi Kappa Psi fraternity considers legal action. Legal analysts suggest individual fraternity members may have grounds for defamation suits, though the university itself cannot sue.

FBI agents captured Kevone Charleston, a suspect in 32 commercial robberies, following a violent confrontation at a Georgia CVS. Two agents were injured when Charleston rammed government vehicles during a pursuit. Charleston was shot and wounded during the arrest; his injuries are non-life-threatening.

Alaska Airlines flight from Seattle to Los Angeles returned to airport after a ramp agent was found asleep in the cargo hold. The employee, who had fallen asleep during loading, was unharmed and discharged from a hospital following a drug test. The airline is investigating the security breach.

A North Carolina judge ruled Monday that Craig Hicks can face the death penalty for the February shooting deaths of three Muslim college students. Hicks is charged with three counts of first-degree murder. Federal authorities are investigating whether the killings constituted a hate crime.

Amnesty International is calling on Afghan authorities to protect women's rights activists following a rise in targeted attacks and persecution. The report highlights government inaction and systemic violence, citing the recent brutal lynching of a young woman in Kabul. Despite the risks, activists report a growing movement of female solidarity and resilience.

New York judge authorizes service of divorce papers via Facebook private messaging. Ruling reflects a shift toward electronic notification as defendants increasingly avoid traditional in-person or mail service.

Rev. Robert H. Schuller, founder of the "Hour of Power" ministry and Crystal Cathedral, died Thursday at 88 from esophageal cancer. A pioneer of televangelism, Schuller was known for his "possibility thinking" and uplifting message of hope. His ministry later faced financial decline and bankruptcy following family succession disputes.

Four workers died and 45 were injured in a massive fire on Pemex's Abkatun Permanente platform off the Mexican coast Wednesday. Approximately 300 people were evacuated before the blaze was extinguished Wednesday night. Pemex reported no oil spill and denied rumors that the platform collapsed.

Kansas Gov. Sam Brownback signed a first-of-its-kind law banning "dismemberment abortion" procedures. The law allows exceptions to protect the mother's life or health. Opponents condemn the measure as dangerous and among the most restrictive in the U.S.

CCTV host Bi Fujian has apologized after a video surfaced of him cursing Chairman Mao Zedong during a dinner party. The state broadcaster is investigating the incident, which has sparked online debate over free speech and political taboos.

University of Kentucky guard Andrew Harrison apologized after a hot mic captured him using a racial slur toward Wisconsin player Frank Kaminsky. Harrison stated the comment was made in jest, and Kaminsky said he has moved past the incident.

Executive producer Brian Grazer announced "Arrested Development" will return for a fifth season of 17 episodes. Netflix has not yet commented on the news. Casting for the new season remains unconfirmed.

CERN has restarted the Large Hadron Collider following a two-year shutdown and final technical tests. The world's largest particle accelerator aims to recreate Big Bang conditions to study dark matter and the origin of mass.

An Iranian observation aircraft flew within 50 yards of a U.S. Navy helicopter over the Persian Gulf in an undisclosed encounter. U.S. officials suspect the unsafe maneuver was a local command error rather than a sanctioned operation. The U.S. administration is considering a formal protest.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev found guilty on all 30 counts in Boston Marathon bombing trial. Defendant now eligible for death penalty following 17 capital convictions. Trial enters penalty phase to determine sentencing.

Four FabIndia employees were arrested in Goa after Education Minister Smriti Irani discovered a surveillance camera overlooking a store changing room. Police charged the staff with voyeurism and breach of privacy. The company is cooperating with authorities and conducting an internal investigation.

Iran will partially lift its long-standing ban on women attending men's sports events within the next year. Deputy Sports Minister Abdolhamid Ahmadi stated the change will primarily apply to indoor events. The move follows international pressure and the loss of a bid to host the 2019 Asian Cup.

Former Satyam Computer Services chairman Ramalinga Raju and nine others sentenced to seven years in prison for a $1.6 billion corporate fraud. The group was convicted of cheating and criminal conspiracy after Raju admitted to inflating profits with fictitious assets. Raju was also ordered to pay an $804,000 fine.

Alaska Airlines removed a cancer patient from a Hawaii-bound flight after she reported feeling weak, citing safety policies regarding medical issues over open ocean. The passenger, Elizabeth Sedway, claimed she was treated like a criminal for lacking a doctor's note. The airline apologized and refunded the family's travel expenses.
Beloved Turkish singer and songwriter Kayahan has died of cancer in an Istanbul hospital at age 66. The artist, known for his love songs and Eurovision appearance, had battled the disease since 1990.

Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu criticized the proposed Iran nuclear deal as "very bad," urging increased pressure to secure better terms. The comments fuel a U.S. political divide, with President Obama and some Democrats defending the framework while Republicans argue it grants Iran too much flexibility.

A suspected kidnapper wounded a security guard at the U.S. Census Bureau before leading police on a chase through Washington. The incident ended in a shootout on H Street, leaving both the suspect and a police officer injured. The kidnapping victim was recovered in good condition.

Imprisoned whistleblower Chelsea Manning has joined Twitter via a third-party communications firm. Manning, serving a 35-year sentence for leaking classified documents to WikiLeaks, lacks direct internet access in prison.

Rapper Nelly was arrested in Tennessee after a state trooper stopped his private bus on Interstate 40. Authorities recovered methamphetamine, marijuana, drug paraphernalia, and several handguns during the search. Nelly faces felony drug possession charges and has since posted bond.

A Delaware father and his two sons fell critically ill after suspected exposure to the restricted pesticide methyl bromide at a U.S. Virgin Islands resort. The EPA is investigating the incident, and the U.S. Department of Justice has launched a criminal probe. The rental agency has terminated its contract with the pest control firm involved.

Authoritarian Asian governments are increasingly using lawsuits, imprisonment, and censorship to silence online dissidents and bloggers. In regions with weak rule of law, such as Bangladesh, online journalists also face deadly attacks from extremist groups. The trend highlights the growing vulnerability of digital media actors operating outside state-controlled channels.
Nina Dobrev will leave "The Vampire Diaries" at the end of the current season. Producers plan to continue the show into a seventh season, sparking backlash from fans.

Yarmouk Palestinian refugee camp faces extreme devastation following an ISIS raid and subsequent Syrian government bombing campaign. Approximately 18,000 residents remain trapped amid severe food and water shortages. UNRWA officials are calling for international intervention to secure civilian safety and aid access.

NASA scientists outline a multi-decade strategy to detect extraterrestrial life using advanced telescopes and planetary probes. While billions of habitable exoplanets suggest primitive life is likely, the odds of contacting intelligent civilizations remain low due to vast distances and timing. Future missions, including the James Webb Space Telescope, will prioritize searching for atmospheric biosignatures.

Carlos Colina, 32, faces murder charges after the remains of 26-year-old Jonathan Camilien were found in a duffel bag and apartment building in Cambridge. Colina was previously arraigned for assault and improper disposal of a body. He is scheduled for arraignment on the murder charge April 14.
Kanye West has settled a civil lawsuit with photographer Daniel Ramos following a 2013 assault at LAX. The settlement included an apology from West and the dismissal of the case prior to trial.

Critics argue President Obama's desire for a legacy achievement has weakened U.S. leverage in nuclear talks with Iran. The resulting framework agreement is viewed as a win for Tehran, allowing it to remain a nuclear threshold state while lifting sanctions too early. This perceived U.S. desperation is reportedly destabilizing the Middle East and prompting regional rivals to consider their own nuclear options.

Officer Michael Slager was arrested for murder after video emerged of him killing unarmed Walter Scott in South Carolina. The incident highlights a critical lack of national data on police killings due to the failure to implement the 1994 Violent Crime Control and Law Enforcement Act. Critics argue mandatory federal data collection is essential to identify racial bias and prevent future abuses.

Five Americans monitored for Ebola exposure in Omaha have been released after testing negative. The clinicians were exposed to a colleague in Sierra Leone. All 17 patients under CDC monitoring are expected to be released by Thursday.

Mark Ronson and Bruno Mars' "Uptown Funk!" has spent 13 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming the longest-leading single of the 2010s. The track also tied a record for the most weeks atop the Digital Songs chart. Newcomer Natalie La Rose entered the top 10 with her debut hit "Somebody."
Fans celebrated "Rex Manning Day" on April 8, referencing the 1995 film Empire Records. The date joins other movie-inspired calendar milestones, including "Mean Girls Day" on October 3.
"Grace of Monaco," starring Nicole Kidman, will premiere on Lifetime on May 25. The Weinstein Co. opted for a direct-to-cable release following poor international performance and critical backlash.

Tokyo's Shibuya ward passed an ordinance Wednesday to issue "partnership certificates" for same-sex couples. The non-binding certificates grant limited rights, including hospital visitation and joint tenancy agreements. Activists view the move as a significant step toward national marriage equality in Japan.

California's prolonged drought has triggered mandatory water cuts and threatens to drive up national produce and beef prices. While a strong dollar and low oil costs may mitigate some inflation, economists warn of potential supply drops. The crisis is also impacting West Coast tourism and agriculture, though wine quality remains high.

University of Michigan will proceed with a screening of "American Sniper" after previously canceling it due to student objections. Officials cited freedom of expression as the reason for reversing the decision.

The 2015 MTV Movie Awards featured highlights including Amy Schumer's opening monologue and a twerking performance by Channing Tatum. Notable misfires included a failed archery gag and an incoherent acceptance speech by Shailene Woodley. Kevin Hart and Robert Downey Jr. also received major honors during the event.

Fiberglass boat debris suspected to be from the 2011 Japan tsunami was towed to Newport, Oregon. The wreckage contained yellowtail jack fish native to Japanese waters. The fish will be transferred to the Oregon Coast Aquarium.

Nigeria marks the first anniversary of the Boko Haram kidnapping of nearly 300 schoolgirls from Chibok. President-elect Muhammadu Buhari pledged an aggressive campaign against the militants as over 200 girls remain missing. Global calls for their return continue under the #BringBackOurGirls campaign.

Article explores the significance of the Easter Triduum, detailing the progression from the suffering of Good Friday to the transformation of Easter Sunday. Author argues the holiday's rituals mirror the universal human experience of moving through darkness toward hope.

Kenya froze 86 bank accounts linked to Al-Shabaab following a university massacre in Garissa that killed 147 people. The government also launched airstrikes on militant camps in Somalia and offered a reward for the attack's alleged organizer. Authorities face criticism over delayed response times despite prior intelligence of the threat.

Entrepreneur Jia Jiang authored the book "Rejection Proof" following a "100 Days of Rejection" project to overcome his fear of failure. Jiang uses his viral experiences to teach others how to demystify rejection and turn it into opportunity.

Attorney General Eric Holder issued a memo prohibiting all Justice Department personnel from soliciting commercial sex, regardless of local legality. The directive follows reports of DEA agents attending cartel-funded sex parties and other misconduct overseas. Violators face suspension or termination.

Police are investigating the killing of a Wayne Community College employee as a possible hate crime. Suspect Kenneth Morgan Stancil III was arrested in Florida after fleeing the North Carolina campus. Investigators are examining if Stancil has ties to a white supremacist gang.

Amnesty International's annual review reports a global decline in executions, though some governments are increasing capital punishment to combat terrorism and crime. The report highlights a rise in death sentences in countries like Pakistan and Egypt amid political instability. Despite these trends, 140 states are now abolitionist in law or practice.

A Duke University student admitted to hanging a noose near a student union Wednesday. The student has been removed from campus pending a conduct review and ongoing criminal investigations. The incident sparked protests and a campus forum condemning the act as hate speech.

Emmy-winning actor Richard Dysart, best known for his role in "L.A. Law," has died at 86. Dysart passed away Sunday at his home in Santa Monica following a long illness. He had a prolific career across stage and screen, including roles in "Wall Street" and "Pale Rider."

Easter celebrations continue globally, with Pope Francis calling for peace during services at the Vatican. The holiday's shifting date is determined by astronomical events and the lunar calendar, leading to differing dates between Western and Orthodox traditions. Secular customs, such as Easter eggs and bunnies, are attributed to historical German traditions.

Comedian Chris Rock sparked social media debate after tweeting about being pulled over by police three times in seven weeks. The posts highlighted "driving while black" and racial profiling, prompting mixed reactions and a suggestion from actor Isaiah Washington to drive less conspicuous cars.

Robert Lewis Burns Jr., original Lynyrd Skynyrd drummer, died Friday night in a single-car crash in Cartersville, Georgia. The 64-year-old musician was unrestrained when his vehicle hit a mailbox and a tree. Burns left the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame band in 1975.

A viral photo of a cat on stairs has sparked a social media debate over whether the animal is moving up or down. The optical illusion, trending via Imgur and 9gag, has drawn comparisons to the #TheDress phenomenon.

US and P5+1 partners reached a framework agreement in Switzerland to limit Iran's nuclear program and prevent weapons development. The deal mandates reduced uranium stockpiles, fewer centrifuges, and permanent IAEA inspection protocols. Proponents argue the agreement exceeds security goals despite expected political opposition in the US.

University of Virginia remains under investigation by the U.S. Department of Education and the state attorney general over its handling of campus sexual assault. Despite the retraction of a sensationalized Rolling Stone story, critics argue the university's failure to expel students for sexual assault persists. Survivors express concern that the journalistic failure may discourage future victims from coming forward.

Indiana Pacers player Chris Copeland and a female companion were stabbed Wednesday morning outside a New York City nightclub. A suspect is in custody, while Atlanta Hawks players Pero Antic and Thabo Sefolosha were arrested for obstruction and disorderly conduct. Copeland is reported to be in stable condition.

Twisted Sister announced their 2016 "Forty and F*ck It" tour will be the band's final outing. The tour marks their 40th anniversary and will feature new drummer Mike Portnoy. The band will also hold two tribute shows for late drummer A.J. Pero.

John Travolta has dismissed the critical HBO documentary "Going Clear: Scientology and the Prison of Belief," stating he has no interest in watching it. The actor defended the Church of Scientology as "brilliant," citing its support during the death of his son.

"Furious 7" earned a record $146 million opening weekend as audiences praised the film's emotional tribute to late actor Paul Walker. Director James Wan opted to retire Walker's character through a sincere montage rather than killing him off. Fans took to social media to describe the final scenes as a fitting and wrenching homage.

HBO's "Game of Thrones" returns for its fifth season, premiering simultaneously in 170 countries. Producers and analysts expect major story arcs to converge and plotlines to advance beyond the original book series.

Rare survival stories highlight the ingenuity and luck of individuals stranded at sea. Recent cases include a fisherman adrift for over a year in the Pacific and others surviving weeks of dehydration and equipment failure. Most such incidents end in death, making these rescues exceptional.
The first six "Star Wars" films launch on digital HD this Friday. The collection includes rare behind-the-scenes features, including a look at sound designer Ben Burtt's process.

Dzhokhar Tsarnaev was found guilty on all 30 counts related to the 2013 Boston Marathon bombings. Victims and families expressed a mix of relief and grief, stating the verdict provides accountability and a step toward closure.

China has formally charged former security czar Zhou Yongkang with bribery, abuse of power, and leaking state secrets. Zhou is the highest-ranking Communist Party official to ever face corruption charges. The case is seen as a key milestone in President Xi Jinping's sweeping anti-corruption campaign.

A Philadelphia woman faces multiple charges after allegedly abandoning her 21-year-old quadriplegic son in Cobbs Creek Park for four days. The man was discovered suffering from dehydration and malnutrition after his mother traveled to Maryland to visit a boyfriend. Police are investigating the woman's history of care and the involvement of social service agencies.

Walmart's opposition to a religious freedom law in Arkansas helped prompt Governor Asa Hutchinson to withhold his signature. The move signals a shift in the retailer's political stance and reflects a broader business community trend against LGBT discrimination. Some Republicans suggest the company's evolution foreshadows a necessary ideological shift for the GOP.

A lapsed Catholic describes returning to faith inspired by Pope Francis's inclusive tone and humility. The author highlights the Pope's focus on the Gospel over judgment, as echoed by Cardinal Gerald Lacroix.

Mary Kay Letourneau and Vili Fualaau will appear in an ABC "20/20" interview to discuss their marriage 10 years after wedding. Letourneau, who served seven years in prison for a relationship with Fualaau when he was 13, plans to seek removal of her sex offender status and return to teaching.

Hillary Clinton has officially announced her 2016 presidential candidacy. The move positions her as a symbolic litmus test for gender equality, though analysts argue partisan politics and economic factors will ultimately determine the outcome.

Amnesty International reports a 22% global decline in executions for 2014, though death sentences rose 28%. The organization warns that governments are increasingly using terrorism threats to justify capital punishment. Report highlights include mass-sentencing in Egypt and Nigeria and continued high execution rates in Iran, Saudi Arabia, and Iraq.

Japan's Defense Minister told parliament that the Air Self Defense Force has never encountered an extraterrestrial UFO. The statement followed an inquiry from lawmaker and former wrestler Antonio Inoki regarding alien threats.

Mark Wahlberg will star in and produce "Patriots' Day," a film about the Boston Marathon bombing told from the perspective of Police Commissioner Ed Davis. Produced by CBS Films, the project will utilize research from "60 Minutes."

Potential Democratic presidential contenders Martin O'Malley and Jim Webb displayed contrasting campaign styles at a Des Moines event Friday. Both face steep uphill battles in polling against frontrunner Hillary Clinton. Webb focused on veterans and governance, while O'Malley emphasized retail politics and economic issues.

Turkish authorities arrested nine British citizens, including four children, for attempting to cross illegally into Syria. The British Foreign Office is seeking further information from Turkey regarding the incident.

US Department of Justice files 15-count indictment against FedEx for conspiracy to transport illegal prescription pharmaceuticals and money laundering. FedEx argues it is exempt from liability as a "common carrier" acting in the usual course of business. The DOJ alleges the company ignored warnings about illegal internet pharmacies using its services.

Kenyans are using social media to honor 147 victims of an Al-Shabaab attack at Garissa University College, the nation's deadliest since 1998. The Islamist group targeted students and security personnel, separating victims by religion during the massacre. One deceased attacker has been identified as the son of a government official.

Photographer Johan Bavman is documenting Swedish fathers utilizing the nation's generous 480-day parental leave program. The project highlights the bonding process and the challenges of full-time childcare to provide realistic role models for men. The series will eventually culminate in a book and exhibition.

President Obama reaffirmed his commitment to maintaining Israel's military edge amid criticism from Prime Minister Netanyahu over the Iran nuclear deal. Obama argued that the agreement provides essential oversight of Iran's nuclear program regardless of trust in Tehran. The U.S. president further pledged American support for Israel against any state attack.

Controversy over Indiana's Religious Freedom Restoration Act has highlighted the broader impact of state and federal religious liberty laws. While critics fear such laws enable discrimination, legal experts note they primarily benefit religious minorities in cases involving sacred items, dietary needs, and ritual substances. Court outcomes remain mixed, with some believers winning protections while others fail to overcome zoning and security regulations.

Five Chinese feminists face up to five years in prison after being detained for planning International Women's Day protests. Prosecutors are considering charges of "assembling a crowd to disturb public order" following campaigns against sexual harassment and domestic violence. The detentions have sparked international condemnation and calls for the women's release.

Selena's family is partnering with Acrovirt LLC to create "Selena the One," a digital embodiment of the late singer. The project aims to release new music and launch a tour in 2018. An Indiegogo campaign to fund the venture begins April 16.

Former Rep. Michele Bachmann drew criticism for comparing President Obama to the pilot who deliberately crashed Germanwings Flight 9525. Bachmann likened the administration's Iran nuclear deal to flying the U.S. "into the rocks." Critics blasted the analogy as inappropriate and disrespectful.

Ryan Gosling's directorial debut "Lost River" hits theaters April 10 following a divisive critical reception. Gosling says the film's "post-industrial gothic" tone was inspired by the decay and resilience of Detroit. The project began as a documentary effort to capture the city's crumbling architecture before demolition.

Yahya Rashid, 19, was charged Wednesday with terror offenses after being arrested at Luton airport upon arrival from Turkey. Rashid faces charges of preparing terrorist acts and assisting others to commit them between November and March.

Mötley Crüe's Vince Neil faced criticism after a poor rendition of the national anthem at a Las Vegas Arena Football League game. The performance follows a history of high-profile musical successes and failures with the song, including Whitney Houston and Roseanne Barr.

WWI soldier graffiti has been discovered in a vast underground city in Naours, France. Photographer Jeff Gusky identified nearly 2,000 names, primarily Australian and British, carved into the chalk quarry. The site was recently opened to the public after decades of private ownership.

The Palestinian Authority officially joined the International Criminal Court Wednesday as its 123rd member. The move grants the court jurisdiction to investigate alleged war crimes in Palestinian territories, including East Jerusalem. Israel and the United States opposed the accession, arguing it is counterproductive to peace.

Anthony Ray Hinton was released Friday after spending nearly 30 years on Alabama's death row for murders he did not commit. Charges were dismissed after firearms evidence failed to link Hinton to the 1985 killings. Attorneys cited the case as a critical example of the need for capital punishment reform.

U.S. taxpayers increasingly view Tax Day as a positive experience due to simplified filing and large average refunds. This "happy ending" masks systemic issues, including tax biases against dual-income couples and advantages for wealthy capital owners.

Jordan Spieth maintained a four-shot lead heading into the final round of the 2015 Masters. Despite surges from Justin Rose, Phil Mickelson, Tiger Woods, and Rory McIlroy, Spieth remained the dominant leader.

Liana Barrientos, 39, pleaded not guilty to criminal charges stemming from an alleged immigration scam involving 10 marriages. Prosecutors claim Barrientos married multiple men simultaneously to help them obtain permanent residency. Barrientos faces up to four years in prison if convicted.

Indiana pizzeria Memories Pizza faces boycotts and arson threats after owners refused to cater a same-sex wedding, citing religious beliefs. Despite the backlash, a crowdfunding campaign raised over $842,000 in support of the business.

Vijay Chokalingam, brother of actress Mindy Kaling, is writing a book about posing as African-American to gain medical school admission. Chokalingam claims the act proves affirmative action provides unfair advantages to minorities. Despite his efforts, he was rejected by most top-tier schools and received only one offer.

Antarctica may have hit a record high of 63.5°F (15.5°C) on March 24 at Argentina's Esperanza Base. The World Meteorological Organization is convening a committee of experts to verify the measurement. Findings are expected by late summer or early fall.

U.S. officials have scrapped the spring timeframe for an Iraqi-led offensive to recapture Mosul from ISIS. Administration officials cited the city's large population and strategic importance as reasons for a more cautious approach. No U.S. combat troops will be involved in the eventual ground operation.

Irish betting firm Paddy Power has deleted a tweet comparing Newcastle United's losses at Anfield to police killings of unarmed African-American men. The company defended the post as a joke, though it continues to face social media backlash.

Philadelphia police added an attempted murder charge against Nyia Parler, who allegedly left her quadriplegic son in a park for four days to visit a boyfriend. Parler was arrested in Maryland and awaits extradition pending the completion of medical treatment. The 21-year-old victim was found dehydrated and malnourished.

South Korean authorities have charged Kim Ki-jong with attempted murder for the March 5 stabbing of U.S. Ambassador Mark Lippert. Kim allegedly attacked the envoy over joint military drills; investigators are probing his previous ties to North Korea.
Jill Dillard, daughter of "19 Kids and Counting" stars Jim Bob and Michelle Duggar, has given birth to a son, Israel David. The baby arrived more than a week past his due date.

Universal's "Furious 7" is projected to debut between $135 million and $138 million in North America, marking the largest domestic opening since fall 2013. The film's worldwide debut could approach or exceed $300 million by Easter Sunday. The release marks the final appearance of the late Paul Walker.

Secret Service supervisor Xavier Morales has been placed on administrative leave following allegations of assault and sexual harassment of a female employee. The incident adds to a series of recent agency scandals, including security lapses at the White House. The Office of the Inspector General is investigating.

Hillary Clinton to announce 2016 presidential candidacy, leveraging extensive experience and political strength. Campaign faces challenges regarding voter authenticity, base motivation, and potential liabilities linked to Bill Clinton. Strategy will focus on direct voter engagement to establish a clear vision and counter "inevitability" perceptions.

DOJ to negotiate restructuring of Ferguson Police Department following findings of systemic racial discrimination and predatory policing. City leadership sees major shifts with the resignation of the police chief and town manager, alongside the election of two Black council members. Activists now seek to ensure fundamental structural reforms to prevent a return to unaccountable governance.

Etihad Airways is investigating after a passenger's cat went missing at New York's JFK Airport following a flight from Abu Dhabi. The owner alleges the pet escaped through a damaged carrier. The airline has hired specialists to assist in the search.

Louis Jordan, 37, was rescued by a container ship after drifting at sea for 66 days in a 35-foot sailboat. Jordan survived the ordeal by collecting rainwater and catching fish using his laundry as bait. He was transported to a Norfolk, Virginia, hospital in surprisingly good physical condition.
